The agent–environment loop

Reinforcement learning is learning from trial and error. An agent acts, the environment responds with a new situation and a number called the reward, and the loop repeats. You are the agent.

🤖 Agent
action → ← state, reward
🌍 Environment

The maths

Time moves in steps $t = 0, 1, 2, \dots$ At each step the agent sees a state $S_t$, picks an action $A_t$, and receives a reward $R_{t+1}$ and the next state $S_{t+1}$. One run from start to finish is an episode. Written out, it is a trajectory:

$$S_0,\ A_0,\ R_1,\ S_1,\ A_1,\ R_2,\ S_2,\ \dots,\ R_T,\ S_T$$

The reward has index $t+1$ because it arrives after the action taken at time $t$. $T$ is the final step.

The agent's goal is to maximise the return, the sum of the rewards it collects:

$$G = R_1 + R_2 + \dots + R_T$$

Under the first reward scheme, every route to the flag has $G = 1$. Under the second, each extra step costs 1, so shorter routes have higher return.
